newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE FIRMS BUY ADDITIONAL 40,000T U.S.WHEAT.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE FIRMS BUY ADDITIONAL 40,000T U.S.WHEAT.

text.p: Philippine firms had bought an additional 40,000 tonnes U.S. wheat, traders said on Thursday.

Traders involved in the deal said the firms bought 5,500 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with 14 percent protein content at $183 to $184 per tonne FOB and 18,500 tonnes dark northern spring wheat with 14 percent protein content at $178 to $179 per tonne FOB.
The firms also bought a total of 16,000 tonnes western white wheat at $153 to $154 per tonne FOB.
On Tuesday, a Philippine mill also bought 27,000 tonnes U.S. wheat after prices dipped to better levels.
Philippine firms have stepped up wheat buying at the start of this month due to softer prices and the slight recovery of the peso, traders said.
Local flour millers bought 100,000 tonnes Canadian wheat and 67,000 tonnes U.S. wheat since August 1.
Philippine wheat buyers were mostly sidelined last month after the peso plunged by more than 11 percent following its de facto devaluation on July 11.
The peso had been rising against the dollar in recent days. It opened at 28.55 on Thursday from the previous day's close of 28.49.
